title: Prosecution ready should VP Sara, Mans Carpio testify in impeachment court - Joel Chua
summary: The prosecution is ready should Vice President Sara Duterte and her husband, Manases Carpio, testify before the impeachment court, House lead prosecutor and Manila 3rd District Representative Joel…

blocks.text: The prosecution is ready should Vice President Sara Duterte and her husband, Manases Carpio, testify before the impeachment court, House lead prosecutor and Manila 3rd District Representative Joel Chua said, as senator-judges aim to secure a verdict before the year ends.

“While we are anticipating that [na haharap si VP Duterte/Atty. Mans Carpio] na possible, dahil kagaya ng sinasabi namin from the very beginning, sila lang ang makakasagot nang lahat ng isyung 'to. Kung sila man ang ipepresenta, naka-ready naman kami,” Chua told Super Radyo dzBB on Sunday.

(While we are anticipating that VP Duterte and Atty. Mans Carpio may appear, as we have been saying from the very beginning, they are the only ones who can answer all these issues. If they are presented as witnesses, we are ready.)

On the 45th day of Duterte’s impeachment trial, defense witness and Trade and Industry Undersecretary Ceferino Rodolfo testified that Cale88 Foods Corp., a listed business interest of Carpio, is a registered micro, small and medium enterprise (MSME) despite millions in money flows.
The Senate impeachment court has moved the trial dates from November 26 and 27 to December 1, 2, 3, and 4 due to the unavailability of defense witnesses.
Chua expressed satisfaction with the witnesses presented by the defense, saying that their testimonoes and actions are helping the prosecution in winning the case.
“Masaya kami sa mga testigo na ipiniprisinta nila dahil sa tingin namin ay maganda naman ang nagiging performance sa pagtulong sa amin,” Chua said.
(We are pleased with the witnesses the defense has presented because we believe they have been performing well in helping our case.)
“So far, nakakailang testigo na sila, so far wala pa silang naiprepresentang substantial,” he added.
(So far, they have presented several witnesses, but they have yet to offer anything substantial.)

He explained that the prosecution's case focuses on the P817 million in allegedly undeclared wealth in Duterte's Statement of Assets, Liabilities, and Net Worth (SALN), not the issue of whether Cale88 is a registered business or not.
“Hindi namin kinukuwestiyon ang pagiging rehistrado ng Cale88. Ang isyu rito ay yung hindi idineklarang income,” Chua said.
(We are not questioning whether Cale88 is registered. The issue here is the income that was not declared.)
“Dahil ang Article 2 ay about unexplained wealth. Walang kaugnayan kung rehistrado 'yan o hindi. Ang pinag-uusapan dito, ito bang kinita sa Cale 88 ay isinama sa SALN,” he added.
(Article 2 is about unexplained wealth. Whether it is registered or not is irrelevant. The question is whether the income earned from Cale88 was included in the SALN.) —RF, GMA News
